findings.title: Scoped searches scan every cached session
findings.suggested_fix: Select separate scoped and global SQL statements. For Some(session), use WHERE d.session=?1 AND instr(d.folded,?2)>0 so the existing (session,seq,part) primary key can seek directly to that session. Preserve the current grouping, limit, revision snapshot, and global-search behavior. Verify equivalent results and indexed scoped access with multiple cached sessions.
findings.why_it_matters: The deployed desktop_session_search always supplies its current session, but the optional-scope OR predicate prevents an index seek. No-match scoped searches walk every cached document index entry, so searching one small session becomes progressively slower as unrelated histories accumulate. This defeats isolation of scoped search cost in the shared cache (up to 4096 sessions); the fix needs no new index or semantic change.
evidence: git diff c139f1f -- native-helper/src/index.rs identifies this as a new file and line 426 as an added optional-scope predicate, so the behavior is introduced by this shipping change.
desktop/native/tools-plugin.mjs:18 passes exec.agent.session.id to index.search; desktop/native/session-text.mjs sends that ID as the search operation session.

On Python SQLite 3.45.3, an in-memory reproduction of the query and primary keys produces EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: SCAN d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1. Replacing only (?1 IS NULL OR d.session=?1) with d.session=?1 produces SEARCH d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1 (session=?).

A bounded in-memory experiment with 100 sessions and 100 short documents each, querying absent in s050 with limit 21, returned identical empty results: current SQL executed 50358 SQLite VM instructions versus 653 for the direct scoped predicate. This measures query work, not production wall-clock latency. No repository, user, or persistent database was modified.

validation.reason: The scoped-search finding is a concrete introduced performance defect, not merely the intentional bounded substring scan. A substring search must examine the selected session's text, but the optional-scope OR causes traversal of unrelated cached sessions too. The shipping tool always supplies its current session, and cache limits allow 4096 sessions and 1 GiB. Separating scoped SQL removes avoidable cache-wide work without changing substring semantics, snapshot revision checks or the schema.
evidence: Independently extracted the exact SQL from native-helper/src/index.rs and reproduced its table definitions in an in-memory Python SQLite 3.45.3 database with 100 sessions and 100 documents each; no repository files or persistent database were modified.

For the same no-match query scoped to s050, current SQL returned no rows and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reported SCAN d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1; it executed 50358 VM instructions. Changing only the optional-scope OR to d.session=?1 returned the same result, reported SEARCH d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1 (session=?), and executed 652 VM instructions.
native-helper/Cargo.toml selects rusqlite bundled SQLite; Cargo.lock pins libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1. Its installed sqlite3/sqlite3.c defines SQLITE_VERSION 3.46.0 at line 462.

Inspected the exact bundled SQLite amalgamation's exprAnalyzeOrTerm at lines 160834-160869 and 160909-160967: usable OR access requires all disjuncts to be indexable for the same table, intersects their table masks, and requires equality terms for OR-to-IN conversion. The parameter-only ?1 IS NULL disjunct is not a document-column constraint. The multi-index OR loop at lines 166687-166689 requires that resulting indexable mask. This supports the same planner limitation in the shipped dependency.

desktop/native/tools-plugin.mjs passes exec.agent.session.id into SessionTextIndex.search, and desktop/native/session-text.mjs includes that session ID in the helper search request. The all-session path exists but is not the shipping tool's normal use.
validation.verification_boundary: VM counts and plans were executed with system SQLite 3.45.3; bundled SQLite 3.46.0 was inspected at source level, not executed in a new harness. This is query-work evidence, not a production wall-clock benchmark. A targeted query-plan check on the bundled version is appropriate when implementing the fix.

verification_queries: SELECT d.session FROM documents d LEFT JOIN sessions s USING(session) WHERE s.session IS NULL LIMIT 1;
SELECT s.session FROM sessions s WHERE s.documents <> (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seq) FROM documents d WHERE d.session=s.session) LIMIT 1;
SELECT session,seq FROM documents GROUP BY session,seq HAVING MIN(part)<>0 OR MAX(part)+1<>COUNT(*) LIMIT 1;
notes.query_caveat: Run optional integrity queries only against the derived cache; quick_check should return ok and invariant queries should return no rows. Do not mutate or migrate official logs or official index databases.

residual_risks: Native activation is deliberately fail-closed on platform, version, or artifact mismatch; in that state the desktop_session_search tool is absent even though official session functionality remains available. This is an operational capability boundary rather than a parity defect in the shipped compatible path.

The activation gate pins the CLI plus session and persistence packages, while desktop-native-tools also imports dsh-session-query and cordis APIs without checking their package versions. The current locked 0.1.2-rc.1 bundle provides the expected APIs, but a selectively modified installation under the same CLI version would rely on fail-safe plugin load behavior rather than an explicit compatibility gate.

Kernel compatibility version 0.1.2-rc.1 is repeated independently in desktop/native/activation.js, persistence.mjs, session-text.mjs, and scripts/deploy-performance.py. The checks currently agree, but an official-kernel upgrade requires coordinated edits across activation, fallback, and deployment paths; a shared generated compatibility manifest would reduce drift.

The native helper protocol number is duplicated between Rust and two JavaScript transports. Current values all equal 1, but there is no single generated contract or mandatory handshake in NativeClient, so a future partial upgrade could fail only after the first real operation.
Successful loaded-image replacement retains `.before-native-*` sibling binaries with no cleanup path; this is bounded per deployment but can accumulate across repeated upgrades.

Rollback trusts any manifest located beneath install/repair-checks; an accidentally selected or locally modified manifest can operate on allowed install/plugin targets, although hash checks limit ordinary stale-manifest damage.

The document-key migration is forward-only inside disposable desktop-native cache. Returning to a helper that expects the legacy document shape may require retiring that derived cache with all helper processes stopped; authoritative session logs remain untouched and official fallback remains available.

Replacing a loaded Windows executable changes the next launch; the current process continues using its retained image. Activation and rollback therefore require verification after a normal restart, without terminating a user session.
Rollback intentionally refuses foreign edits and tampered backups. Preserve the manifest, byte backups and journal-owned retained images until recovery and post-restart verification are complete.
The migration journal supports process interruption, but its writes are not explicitly fsync-backed; sudden power loss durability was not established by the inspected interruption tests.
testing_gaps: The reviewed tests exercise traversal and request/slice bounds, but do not cover Windows junction/reparse-point containment or a second-session argument attempting to override desktop_session_search's caller-derived scope. Static inspection found both boundaries enforced; this leaf pass did not execute additional tests.

The scoped-query finding is independently validated, but its fix should include a targeted query-plan/result check against bundled SQLite 3.46.0; this review executed system SQLite 3.45.3 and inspected the bundled planner source.

Final source-to-built-artifact hashes, NSIS bundle inspection, actual installation and post-restart runtime evidence remain pending with the parent release workflow. These are release evidence gates, not asserted code defects.
